title: Scene parameters schema
purpose: The synthesis format: what scene.hpp accepts, and what a generator must emit. This file is the single source of truth for the format, and ppm-prompt builds its system prompt from it -- so changing the format means changing this file, not the generator.
why_parameters_and_not_code: Nothing executes generated output. A scene is data, validated on load, so a bad generation is a rejected file rather than a running program.

Every render is reproducible and editable. The parameters that produced a video are written beside it, so it can be re-rendered at another resolution or hand-tweaked without re-running analysis or a model.
All three CLIs converge on one representation, so an analysis-derived scene and a model-generated scene are the same kind of object and can be diffed, merged, or interpolated.

animation.rule: ANY numeric parameter may be either a constant or an animation object. This is what keeps the schema flat -- there is no separate keyframe block that has to be kept in sync with the layers it refers to.

fields.easing: one of the easings listed below; an unknown name degrades to linear rather than failing
fields.loop: true ping-pongs the value so it returns to `from` at phase 1, which is what makes a clip loop seamlessly

animation.phase: Every animation is driven by phase = frame / frames, in [0,1). Nothing reads wall-clock time, which is why renders are reproducible.

fields.samples: NxN supersampling per pixel, 1..8. Cost is samples squared.

output.limits: width * height must not exceed 80 megapixels; samples must be 1..8. Both are rejected at load rather than after allocating.

background.note: The base colour layers composite onto. Defaults to black.

tone.note: Applied after all layers, in this fixed order: exposure, temperature, tonemap, saturation, contrast, vignette, black_floor. The order matters -- black_floor is last so it is not multiplied away by the vignette.

fields.temperature: -1 cool .. +1 warm. Trims red against blue.
fields.tonemap: "none" | "tanh" | "reinhard". Use tanh or reinhard whenever layers ADD, because sums exceed 1 and a hard clip flat-clips highlights to white.
fields.vignette: 0..1 radial darkening. About 0.35 focuses attention without reading as a filter.
fields.black_floor: lifts the darkest value. 0.01-0.03 keeps shadows from reading as holes and makes banding visible enough to fix.

transform.note: A global camera move applied to the sampling coordinates. Zoom and rotate act about the frame centre.

fields.rotate: turns, so 0.25 is a quarter turn

transform.warning: For a reconstructed VIDEO the motion is already present in the per-frame essence grids, so a transform here would double it. It is the right place for motion only when synthesising, or when animating a single still.

layers.note: Composited in order, first is bottom. Each has type, blend, opacity and a type-specific params object.

reconstruct.purpose: Expand a measured essence grid back to full resolution. The core of ppm-video and ppm-media.

params.detail: 0..1, procedural texture standing in for frequencies the grid discarded. Multiplied internally by the MEASURED high_freq_ratio, so a flat source gets no invented texture however high this is set.
params.scale: detail frequency; should track the grid size, because what was lost is the band finer than the grid

reconstruct.note: Requires essence grids supplied by the tool. A generated scene cannot use this type -- there is nothing to reconstruct.

params.colors: array of [r,g,b], interpolated in linear light

params.scale: how quickly the ramp is traversed

fbm.purpose: Fractal noise; the workhorse for clouds, smoke, marble, terrain.

params.scale: frequency, roughly cycles across the half-height. 1 broad, 2.4 default, 6 detailed.
params.warp: domain-warp strength. The cheapest route from bland noise to something structural; 0.85 is a good default.
params.count: octaves, 3 cheap to 8 rich. Cost is linear, and a CPU can afford more than a GPU.
params.seed: decorrelates one fbm layer from another
params.colors: array of [r,g,b] used as a ramp

worley.purpose: Cellular / Voronoi texture: scales, cracks, bubbles, caustics.

grain.purpose: Per-frame noise. Reseeded every frame, so it reads as film rather than as a dirty lens.

params.detail: amplitude; 0.01-0.05 is subtle, above 0.1 is heavy

vignette.purpose: A vignette as a layer, for when it should sit under later layers rather than over everything.
vignette.note: Use blend "multiply". For a simple final vignette, prefer tone.vignette.

authoring_guidance.note: Advice for producing a scene that reads as deliberate. None of it is enforced.
items: Build in layers, bottom-up: a background wash, one or two structural layers, then grain and vignette. Three to five layers is usually enough; more tends to turn to mud.

If any layer uses blend "add" or "screen", set tone.tonemap to "tanh" or "reinhard". Additive layers exceed 1 and a hard clip flat-clips highlights to white, which is the most reliable tell of a careless render.
Keep tone.black_floor at 0.01-0.03. Pure black reads as a hole.
Give at least one parameter an animation, or the clip is a still. Motion in scale, warp or transform.zoom reads as alive; motion in colour usually reads as a glitch.
For a seamless loop set "loop": true on every animation, so each value returns to its start.
Take colours from a coherent palette rather than picking them independently. docs/design-tokens.json has tuned cosine palettes; a 2-3 colour ramp from dark to bright is a reliable default.
Prefer few strong ideas over many weak ones. One well-warped fbm beats four competing textures.
